$comment: The launchd jobs bin/gen-launchd renders to scheduled/*.plist.tmpl. Edit this file,
then run bin/gen-launchd. The schema is at the top of bin/gen-launchd-lib.js.

jobs.label: com.danielhunter.pr-dash
why: Definition only — this file is outside `home/`, so chezmoi never deploys it.
Kept out of the source root for a reason specific to launchd: it reads a plist only at
bootstrap, so an auto-deployed copy means `chezmoi apply` rewrites the file while the
loaded job keeps the old definition. A port or a path change then looks applied and is
not. Rendering by hand makes re-activation an explicit step instead of a skipped one.
A TEMPLATE, so activation renders it rather than symlinking it. launchd expands nothing
in a plist — not $HOME, not ~ — and both ProgramArguments and StandardOutPath have to be
absolute, so a hardcoded /Users/daniel would work on one machine under one account.
Activate on a machine that wants the dashboard always listening on 127.0.0.1:8770:
mkdir -p -m 700 ~/.local/state/pr-dash
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
The mkdir is not optional: launchd creates the log file but not its parent, and the
payload store only creates that directory after the process has already spawned. Mode
700 matches DIR_MODE in src/payload-store.ts — the directory holds private PR titles,
and this host's `umask 0007` would otherwise leave it group-writable.
Deactivate:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.danielhunter.pr-dash"
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
What that costs: the bookmark stops working, since nothing holds the port any more.
`pr-dash` in a terminal still starts a server and opens the browser on it.
Reload after editing this file. launchd read the old definition at bootstrap and will
keep serving it until the job is replaced, so this is the step whose absence makes an
edit look applied when it is not:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.danielhunter.pr-dash"
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.danielhunter.pr-dash.plist
Check it:
launchctl print "gui/$(id -u)/com.danielhunter.pr-dash"
tail -f ~/.local/state/pr-dash/agent.log
The same reload block is what a code change needs. `chezmoi apply` deploys new `public/`
assets under the running server, which serves them per request, while `src/` stays at
whatever the process loaded — so a change to the /api/prs response shape leaves a new
app.js validating an old server's body. That is a 60-second poll and a give-up banner
for up to the 16-hour idle window, which daily use may never reach, so reloading the job
is the fix rather than waiting it out.

ProgramArguments: Reached through fnm's aliases/default symlink, not a version-pinned path, so an
fnm upgrade does not silently strand this agent on a removed Node version.
env.PR_DASH_WORK_ORGS: The GitHub owners whose repositories the dashboard shows by default; everything
else is hidden until the Personal chip is on. Comma-separated, and the name
itself stays out of this repo, which is public-posture: it comes from
[data]. Rendering on a machine that sets no such key emits an empty string,
which src/main-lib.ts's parseWorkOrgs reads as no work organizations at all —
every repository then counts as work and the chip stays hidden.
env.PR_DASH_EXTENSION_ORIGINS: The Chrome extension origins allowed to read the routes in src/server.ts's EXTENSION_PATHS cross-origin,
comma-separated, each chrome-extension://<32-letter id>. The ID stays out of this repo: it comes
from `prDashExtensionOrigins` in the machine-local chezmoi.toml, under [data].
Unset renders an empty string, which accepts no extension origin, and a malformed
entry makes src/main.ts exit at startup rather than serve a wider boundary than
configured. launchd reads this only at bootstrap, so a changed key needs the
reload block in this file's header, not just `chezmoi apply`.
env.PR_DASH_VULN_REPOS: The repositories the vulnerabilities page (/vulns.html) lists open Dependabot alerts
for, comma-separated owner/name. The names stay out of this repo: they come from
`prDashVulnRepos` in the machine-local chezmoi.toml, under [data]. Unset renders an
empty string, and the page then says no repositories are configured. A malformed
entry makes src/main.ts exit at startup rather than silently drop a repository.
The token needs Dependabot-alert read access on each one, or that repository shows
env.PATH: src/token.ts invokes `op` by bare name through execFile, and launchd's default
PATH is just /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin. Without /opt/homebrew/bin here, the
first /api/prs comes back as a 500 carrying an ENOENT.
KeepAlive: Bare <true/>, never a dict with SuccessfulExit <false/>. The idle exit (main-lib.ts's
createIdleExit) exits status 0 by design. Under SuccessfulExit: false, launchd reads
a clean exit as "do not restart", so the port would go dead until the next login and
nothing in this suite would notice.
ThrottleInterval: launchd's own default, named explicitly so the dependency is visible rather than
inherited. It bounds how long the port sits unheld after an idle exit.

jobs.label: com.daniel.retention-sweep
why: The macOS half of the hourly retention sweep. Linux runs it as
home/dot_config/systemd/user/retention-sweep.{service,timer}; this is the same job, with
the same one argument, which tells the sweeper to act. It is the only thing that prunes
~/.claude/artifacts here: manifest rows G20 and G21 replaced the SessionStart hook
prune-artifacts.sh.
Acting covers every APPLY_ROWS row, not only the artifact rows. That includes G14 and
G15, which prune known /tmp prefixes older than a day.
Definition only. Like its siblings it lives outside `home/`, so chezmoi never deploys it
and the job runs only on a machine that activates it by hand.
The label is com.daniel.retention-sweep, outside com.daniel.claude.*, because
work-laptop-config's catch-up.sh globs that prefix and runs `eval` on
ProgramArguments.2. Here that element is the sweeper's path, so a replay would run the
sweep outside its launcher. RunAtLoad covers a missed hour instead.
Activate:
chezmoi execute-template \
< ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scheduled/com.daniel.retention-sweep.plist.tmpl \
> ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.retention-sweep.plist
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" \
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.retention-sweep.plist
Deactivate:
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.daniel.retention-sweep"
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.daniel.retention-sweep.plist
Check it: the last line of the log reports what the last run pruned, and
~/.claude/.retention-sweep-last-run holds the same counts as JSON.

ProgramArguments: Started through run-python.sh, under the uv-managed Python 3.14 the hooks use.
The sweeper's own #!/usr/bin/env python3 resolves to Apple's /usr/bin/python3 on
launchd's PATH, which is 3.9 and lacks os.path.realpath(strict=), so every
env.PATH: Puts uv on PATH for run-python.sh's interpreter lookup. When that lookup fails it
falls back to python3, which this PATH resolves to Homebrew's rather than 3.9.
StartInterval: Hourly, as the systemd timer's OnCalendar=hourly. RunAtLoad stands in for its
Persistent=true: launchd has no catch-up for a machine that was asleep.
